derivations.title: Electric Field on Axial Line of an Electric Dipole
steps: Place dipole -q and +q separated by 2a along the dipole axis
Calculate field due to -q and +q at point P distance r from centre
Take vector difference: E = E_+q - E_-q along dipole moment vector
Apply binomial approximation for short dipole (r >> a)

derivations.title: Electric Field on Equatorial Line of Dipole
steps: Draw symmetric triangle with charges at -a and +a, point P at height r
Decompose fields into cos theta (axial) and sin theta (normal) components
Notice sin theta components cancel completely by symmetry
Sum cos theta components: E = 2 E_1 \cos\theta pointing antiparallel to p

derivations.title: Gauss's Theorem: Field due to Infinitely Long Straight Wire
steps: Choose coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r and length L
Flux through flat circular ends is zero (E perpendicular to area vector)
Curved surface flux = E * (2 * pi * r * L)
By Gauss's Law: E (2*pi*r*L) = (lambda * L) / epsilon_0 => E = lambda / (2*pi*epsilon_0*r)

derivations.title: Gauss's Theorem: Field due to Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet
steps: Construct cylindrical pillbox perpendicular to sheet of cross-section A
Curved surface contributes zero flux (E parallel to surface)
Total flux through two circular ends = 2 * E * A
Charge enclosed q = sigma * A => 2 E A = (sigma * A) / epsilon_0 => E = sigma / (2*epsilon_0)

derivations.title: Capacitance of Parallel Plate Capacitor with Dielectric Slab
steps: Original uniform field in air E0 = sigma / epsilon0
Dielectric slab of thickness t reduces field inside to E = E0 / K
Potential difference V = E0 (d - t) + E t = E0 [d - t + t/K]
Use C = Q / V to obtain final formula

derivations.title: Relation between Current and Drift Velocity & Ohm's Law Deduction
derivations.formula: I = n e A v_d \quad \text{and} \quad \rho = \frac{m}{n e^2 \tau}
steps: Volume of conductor of length l is V = A * l
Total mobile charge in conductor Q = n * e * A * l
Time taken by electrons to drift through t = l / v_d
Current I = Q / t = n e A v_d
Substitute v_d = (e E tau) / m to deduce Ohm's law V = I R

derivations.title: Biot-Savart Law: Magnetic Field on Axis of Circular Current Loop
steps: Take current element dl on ring perimeter of radius R
dB = (mu_0 / 4pi) * (I dl / r^2) where r = sqrt(R^2 + x^2)
Resolve dB into dB_x (along axis) and dB_perp (perpendicular to axis)
dB_perp cancels by symmetry; integrate dB_x over full circular loop

derivations.title: Force Between Two Parallel Current-Carrying Conductors
steps: Field due to conductor 1 at conductor 2: B1 = (mu_0 * I_1) / (2*pi*d)
Force on length L of conductor 2: F2 = I_2 * L * B_1 * sin(90 deg)
Like currents attract; opposite currents repel (Official CBSE 1A definition)

derivations.title: Motional EMF Induced in a Rod Moving in Magnetic Field
steps: Consider conducting rod PQ of length l moving with velocity v in field B
Magnetic Lorentz force on charge q is F = q (v x B)
Work done moving charge along rod W = F * l = q * v * B * l
Induced EMF = W / q = B * v * l

derivations.title: Mutual Inductance of Two Co-axial Long Solenoids
steps: Inner solenoid 1 has radius r1, turns n1; outer solenoid 2 has n2
Current I2 in outer solenoid produces uniform field B2 = mu_0 * n2 * I2
Magnetic flux linked with solenoid 1: Phi1 = N1 * B2 * A1 = (n1 * l)(mu_0 * n2 * I2)(pi * r1^2)
By definition Phi1 = M * I2 => M = mu_0 * n1 * n2 * pi * r1^2 * l

derivations.title: Series LCR Circuit: Impedance & Resonant Frequency
steps: Draw phasor diagram with current phasor I_0 along x-axis
V_R is in phase with I, V_L leads by 90 deg, V_C lags by 90 deg
Resultant voltage V_0^2 = V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2 = I_0^2 [R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2]
At resonance X_L = X_C => omega * L = 1 / (omega * C) => f_r = 1 / (2*pi*sqrt(L*C))

derivations.title: Lens Maker's Formula for a Thin Convex Lens
steps: Refraction at first surface (radius R1): (mu / v1) - (1 / u) = (mu - 1) / R1
Refraction at second surface (radius R2): (1 / v) - (mu / v1) = (1 - mu) / R2
Add equations: (1 / v) - (1 / u) = (mu - 1) * (1 / R1 - 1 / R2)
For u = infinity, v = f, yielding the Lens Maker's formula

derivations.title: Refraction Through a Triangular Prism & Minimum Deviation
steps: For prism: A = r1 + r2 and Deviation D = (i + e) - A
At minimum deviation: i = e and r1 = r2 = r
Then r = A / 2 and D_m = 2i - A => i = (A + D_m) / 2
Apply Snell's law mu = sin(i) / sin(r) to obtain prism equation

derivations.title: Huygens' Principle: Proof of Laws of Reflection & Refraction
steps: Incident plane wavefront AB hits boundary at angle i
Secondary wavelet from A travels to C in time t (distance = v * t)
Draw envelope from B to contact point D
Use congruent/similar right triangles to prove laws geometrically

derivations.title: Young's Double Slit Experiment: Fringe Width Expression
steps: Path difference between waves from slits S1 and S2: delta x = S2 P - S1 P
Using geometry: (S2 P)^2 - (S1 P)^2 = 2 y d => delta x approx (y * d) / D
Condition for bright fringes: delta x = n * lambda => y_n = (n * lambda * D) / d
Fringe width beta = y_{n+1} - y_n = (lambda * D) / d

derivations.title: Bohr's Postulate: Radius and Energy of Orbit in Hydrogen Atom
derivations.formula: r_n = \frac{n^2 h^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi m e^2} \quad \text{and} \quad E_n = -\frac{13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV}
steps: Centripetal force = Electrostatic attraction: (m v^2) / r = (1 / 4 pi epsilon_0) * (e^2 / r^2)
Bohr's quantization postulate: m v r = (n h) / (2 pi) => v = (n h) / (2 pi m r)
Substitute v to solve for radius r_n proportional to n^2
Total energy E = K + U = -e^2 / (8 pi epsilon_0 r) = -13.6 / n^2 eV

namedReactions.title: Sandmeyer Reaction
namedReactions.equation: Ar-N_2^+ X^- + Cu_2Cl_2 / HCl \rightarrow Ar-Cl + N_2
namedReactions.reagents: Cu2Cl2/HCl or Cu2Br2/HBr
namedReactions.significance: Key method to synthesize chlorobenzene and bromobenzene from aniline diazonium salts with high yield

namedReactions.title: Finkelstein Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: NaI in dry acetone (nucleophilic halide exchange)
namedReactions.significance: Halogen exchange specifically designed for synthesizing alkyl iodides; NaCl/NaBr precipitate drives equilibrium forward

namedReactions.title: Swarts Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: Metallic fluorides (AgF, Hg2F2, CoF2, SbF3)
namedReactions.significance: Best laboratory synthesis method for alkyl fluorides via metal fluoride exchange

namedReactions.title: Wurtz-Fittig & Fittig Reactions
namedReactions.reagents: Sodium metal in dry ether
namedReactions.significance: Coupling of aryl halide with alkyl halide (Wurtz-Fittig) or two aryl halides (Fittig) to form biphenyl compounds

namedReactions.title: Kolbe's Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: 1. NaOH 2. CO2 gas (weak electrophile) 3. Dilute H2SO4/HCl
namedReactions.significance: Industrial conversion of phenol to 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid), direct precursor for Aspirin

namedReactions.title: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: Chloroform (CHCl3) + 3 NaOH (generates :CCl2 dichlorocarbene)
namedReactions.significance: Electrophilic formylation yielding ortho-salicylaldehyde as the major board exam product

namedReactions.title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
namedReactions.reagents: Primary alkyl halide + Sodium alkoxide (SN2 mechanism)
namedReactions.significance: Preparation of symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers. Board rule: Alkyl halide MUST be 1° to prevent elimination

namedReactions.title: Rosenmund Reduction
namedReactions.equation: R-COCl + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd / BaSO_4, \, S} R-CHO + HCl
namedReactions.reagents: Pd poisoned with BaSO4 and sulfur/quinoline
namedReactions.significance: Selective catalytic reduction of acyl chlorides to aldehydes without over-reducing to alcohols

namedReactions.title: Stephen Reaction
namedReactions.equation: R-CN + SnCl_2 + HCl \rightarrow R-CH=NH \cdot HCl \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} R-CHO
namedReactions.reagents: SnCl2 + conc. HCl followed by steam hydrolysis
namedReactions.significance: Reduction of nitriles to imines followed by acidic hydrolysis to yield aldehydes

namedReactions.title: Etard Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: Chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2 or CCl4 solvent
namedReactions.significance: Direct controlled mild oxidation of methylbenzene (toluene) to benzaldehyde

namedReactions.title: Gattermann-Koch Reaction
namedReactions.equation: Benzene + CO + HCl \xrightarrow{anhyd.\,AlCl_3 / CuCl} Benzaldehyde + HCl
namedReactions.reagents: Carbon monoxide + HCl in presence of anhydrous AlCl3
namedReactions.significance: Industrial formylation of benzene ring directly to benzaldehyde

namedReactions.title: Clemmensen Reduction
namedReactions.reagents: Zinc amalgam (Zn-Hg) and concentrated hydrochloric acid
namedReactions.significance: Reduction of carbonyl group into methylene under acidic conditions

namedReactions.title: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
namedReactions.reagents: Hydrazine (NH2NH2) followed by heating with KOH in ethylene glycol
namedReactions.significance: Reduction of carbonyl into methylene under strongly basic conditions (ideal for acid-sensitive substrates)

namedReactions.title: Aldol Condensation & Cross Aldol
namedReactions.reagents: Dilute NaOH or Ba(OH)2 + Heat
namedReactions.significance: Self or cross condensation of aldehydes/ketones possessing at least one alpha-hydrogen to form alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyls

namedReactions.title: Cannizzaro Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: Concentrated alkali (50% NaOH or KOH)
namedReactions.significance: Self oxidation-reduction (disproportionation) of aldehydes lacking alpha-hydrogens (e.g. Formaldehyde, Benzaldehyde)

namedReactions.title: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction
namedReactions.reagents: Halogen (Cl2 or Br2) in presence of small amount of red phosphorus
namedReactions.significance: Alpha-halogenation of aliphatic carboxylic acids containing an alpha-hydrogen

namedReactions.title: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
namedReactions.reagents: Phthalimide, ethanolic KOH, primary alkyl halide, aq. NaOH
namedReactions.significance: Best method for synthesizing pure primary aliphatic amines without secondary or tertiary contamination

namedReactions.title: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
namedReactions.equation: R-CONH_2 + Br_2 + 4 NaOH \rightarrow R-NH_2 + Na_2CO_3 + 2 NaBr + 2 H_2O
namedReactions.reagents: Bromine in aqueous or ethanolic NaOH
namedReactions.significance: Step-down reaction: converts an acid amide into a primary amine with ONE LESS carbon atom

namedReactions.title: Carbylamine Test (Isocyanide Test)
namedReactions.equation: R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3 alc.\,KOH \xrightarrow{\Delta} R-NC + 3 KCl + 3 H_2O
namedReactions.reagents: Chloroform and alcoholic KOH with heat
namedReactions.significance: Diagnostic chemical test for primary amines; releases an unmistakable foul odor of isocyanide

namedReactions.title: Hinsberg Test for Amines
namedReactions.reagents: Benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) + alkali
namedReactions.significance: Distinguishes 1° amine (ppt soluble in alkali), 2° amine (ppt insoluble in alkali), 3° amine (does not react)

formulas.notes: Prioritize choice of u using ILATE rule (Inverse, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential)
